evidence.curator_note: Generic scheme R-CR2-YR(+.) -> R. + CR2=YR(+), reaction arrow labelled alpha. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn (the odd electron on Y into the forming C=Y bond, and one electron of the R-CR2 sigma bond into that same bond), move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page; the book simply writes R. as a product). Instantiated by the curator as Y = NH, R = CH3 (N-methylethylamine molecular ion, n-ionized at nitrogen -- the site the book ranks highest for radical-site initiation: N > S, O, pi, R. > Cl, Br > H). The page prints no m/z, no intensity and no specific compound for this scheme.

rule_index cross-links equation 4.9 to IMS_4_9 ([C]1[C]2[C]3([C]4)[_A+.]5 >> [C.]1.[C]2[C]3([C]4){=}[_A+.]5). VERIFIED MISMATCH, not support: (i) the DFS chain is C1-C2-C3(C4)-Y5, so the cleaved bond C1-C2 is NOT incident to the atom C3 that forms the new pi bond -- one carbon too far from Y, whereas the book's alpha-carbon carries both the leaving R and Y (the intended DFS was almost certainly [C]1[C]2([C]3)([C]4)[_A+.]5, i.e. a missing branch parenthesis); (ii) the product keeps [_A+.], so the rule invents a second unpaired electron (spin 1 -> 2) instead of pairing the radical into the pi bond. Checked in the container: the rule matches neither acetone, diethyl ether nor this amine ion; on 2-methoxy-2-methylbutane M+. it does fire and yields [CH2]C(C)(C)=[O+.]C -- a pentavalent carbon and a di-radical product. It is also dropped at assembly time by the conservation guardrail in rules/__init__.py ('4.9 ... [spin 1->2]'), so no live rule reproduces this equation. All m/z values in this record are curator-computed from the chosen instantiation.

The page prints no m/z and no relative intensity for this generic scheme; 44.0495 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of CH2=N(H)+-CH3 for the chosen instantiation (electron-mass corrected, matching utils.term_transfers.exact_mass_from_term). Not a measurement.
